name: Mexico
headline_status: Recreational cannabis use is constitutionally protected in Mexico and possession of up to 5 g is not a crime, but there is no legal market and selling remains a serious offence.
summary: Mexico's Supreme Court struck down the ban on adult recreational use in 2021 through a general declaration of unconstitutionality, but Congress never passed a law to regulate a market. Adults can apply to the health regulator Cofepris for individual permits to grow and possess cannabis for their own use, while possession of up to 5 g is treated as personal consumption. In February 2026 the Court fell one vote short of scrapping the 5 g threshold nationwide, so larger amounts can still lead to prosecution.

adult_use_since.value: June 2021, when the Supreme Court decriminalised adult recreational use (General Declaration of Unconstitutionality 1/2018); no commercial regulation followed.

possession_limit.value: 5 g is the legal threshold for personal consumption; more may trigger an investigation if there are signs of dealing, and the Supreme Court left the limit in place in February 2026.

home_grow.value: Allowed only for adults holding an individual Cofepris permit, which covers growing, harvesting, preparing, possessing and transporting cannabis for the holder's own use.

retail_sales.value: None. Selling, distributing and supplying recreational cannabis remain illegal.

penalties.value: Drug trafficking or dealing can bring 10 to 25 years in prison.

regulator.value: Federal Commission for the Protection against Sanitary Risks (Cofepris).

tourists.value: Visitors have no legal place to buy cannabis; the 5 g personal-use threshold applies to everyone, and self-use permits are issued only to named individual holders.

timeline.event: Chamber of Deputies passes a cannabis regulation bill (28 g, six plants) that never became law
Supreme Court declares the ban on adult recreational use unconstitutional
Supreme Court First Chamber rules prosecutors cannot charge a consumer for possessing over 5 g for personal use (single case)
Supreme Court falls one vote short of removing the 5 g limit with general effect
Cofepris clarifies that self-use permits do not allow any sales

faq.a: Personal use is protected by court rulings and up to 5 g is treated as personal possession, but there are no legal stores and selling is a serious crime.

faq.q: Can tourists buy weed in Mexico?
faq.a: No. There is no legal market, so any purchase is illegal, and carrying more than 5 g can lead to an investigation.

faq.q: Can you grow cannabis in Mexico?
faq.a: Only with an individual self-use permit from Cofepris, which covers growing and possessing cannabis for the holder's own use.
